title: Normalized derived reductions of the actual integral Tate tensor
statement: For every Noetherian scheme T, prime ell invertible on T, and d in N, there exist an AdicTower M for datum ell, level isomorphisms e to derivedRealization of finiteTwist, and h:M.tower=strictDerivedTower T ell d. They satisfy ProjectionNormalized. For every b>=a there exists a generator-normalized CoefficientLineComparison of the finite root lines, and the scalarComparison/proTwistMap square equals M.normalization for every such comparison. This asserts neither a uniform model nor constructibility nor reconstruction. Use the actual objects of [def-pur-condensed-tate-integral-tower-data] and [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower].

proof.text: On the compatible primitive-root covering, identify the completed root module with the completed coefficient unit by sending a compatible residue family to the corresponding powers of the compatible roots. The actual projections are residue followed by the finite root generator. Use the fixed residue and completion isomorphisms and iterate sheaf tensor balancing to identify the d-fold integral quotient with the finite ordinary root tensor. At zero use coefficient multiplication. The arbitrary-scalar formula is exactly ProjectionBalanced and hence glues.

The integral and finite lines are K-flat in their single degree: slice restriction is exact and commutes with tensor; on a trivializing cover tensor with a line preserves acyclic complexes. Vanishing of cohomology descends. Derived quotients are therefore computed by the ordinary balanced quotients, including the shift by 2d.

Take the quotient-linear derived levels of the shifted integral line. Exact evaluation of the strict ordinary quotient tower gives evaluation, and balanced derived quotients give normalization. Their semilinear adjuncts are the strict transitions by the scalar adjunction formula. On pure tensors two successive reductions multiply the same quotient scalars as direct reduction; this proves transition and cocycle, including repeated indices, so the data form AdicTower. Identify the levels through finiteModelIso. The single-complex evaluation formula and ProjectionBalanced give ProjectionNormalized.

For each comparable pair, the root power map followed by scalar extension is the unit isomorphism on primitive-root bases; it therefore gives a CoefficientLineComparison, with its derived component the scalar counit followed by the single sheaf comparison. Any other normalized comparison agrees on scalar/root generators and so has the same sheaf and derived map. Tensor factor by factor, using coefficient multiplication at d=0, and take the specified site/scalar adjunction mates: the resulting proTwistMap squares are exactly the tower normalization squares.

from.place: Step 2: realize the normalized Tate-unit system with common bounds and stratification

lean.statement:
theorem normalizedTateTensorTower_core
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian T] (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime]
    (hT : IsUnit (ell : Γ(T, ⊤))) (d : ℕ) :
    ∃ (M : AdicTower T (datum.{u} ell))
      (e : ∀ n : ℕ, M.level n ≅ (derivedRealization T ell n).obj (finiteTwist T ell n d))
      (h : M.tower = strictDerivedTower T ell d),
      ProjectionNormalized T ell hT d M e h ∧
      (∀ (b a : ℕ) (hab : a ≤ b), Nonempty
        (CoefficientLineComparison
          (FiniteReduction.quotient.{u} ell (Nat.add_le_add_right hab 1))
          (ell ^ (b + 1)) (ell ^ (a + 1))
          (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) T)) ∧
        (∀ (b a : ℕ) (hab : a ≤ b)
          (r : CoefficientLineComparison
            (FiniteReduction.quotient.{u} ell (Nat.add_le_add_right hab 1))
            (ell ^ (b + 1)) (ell ^ (a + 1))
            (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) T),
          (pbcDerivedExtend (pbcAdicQuotient T (datum.{u} ell) b a hab)).map (e b).hom ≫
              (scalarComparison T ell b a hab).hom.app (finiteTwist T ell b d) ≫
              (derivedRealization T ell a).map (proTwistMap d r) =
            (M.normalization b a hab).hom ≫ (e a).hom)
